newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Asia, US trade houses in Australia wheat sale.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Asia, US trade houses in Australia wheat sale.

text.p: Japanese and Chinese trading houses confirmed on Tuesday that they had taken leading roles in Australia's 112,000 tonnes white wheat sale to Pakistan.
Japanese-owned Nichimen Australia Ltd confirmed it had sold 45,000 tonnes of Australian Standard White (ASW) wheat to Pakistan as part of Australia's component in the latest tender.
Chinese-owned CITIC Food Australia confirmed that it had sold 45,000 tonnes at US$156.285 a tonne.

Cargill Australia, part of the American-owned trading giant Cargill Inc was not immediately available for comment on reports that it had also sold part of Australia's component in the Pakistan tender.
The Australian Wheat Board earlier told Reuters that Australia had sold 112,000 tonnes to Pakistan in that country's tender for 315,000 tonnes of white wheat for February delivery.
Nichimen Australia, part of Nichimen Corp, declined to confirm reports that the price in its ASW sale to Pakistan was US$155.30 a tonne.

For CITIC Australia, part of China's state-owned but capitalist CITIC trading group, the sale represents the group's first successful foray into the bulk grains trade, although it has been involved in earlier containerised sales.

Australian trade sources said the U.S. component of the Pakistan tender, sold at between US$150.90 and $152.44 a tonne, was price-equivalent to the Australian sale after freight and financing differentials.
